I am 57 years old and have farmed this land in Quzhou County since I was a young girl. I never went to school, but I know my fields well, and I know what works here on the North China Plain. Every year I watch what my neighbors do and listen to the advice at the village supply store. I have about 8 mu of land in total.

This year, I will stick to the wheat–maize rotation on 6 mu because that is the safest way to put food on the table and earn a little cash. I will sow winter wheat in October after rotary tilling the soil. I will use the improved variety *luyuan502* — about 30 jin per mu — because it yields well and resists lodging. I will spread compound fertilizer as a basal dressing and top-dress with urea in the spring. The wheat needs four irrigations: one before winter to help it survive the cold, and three more in spring when the grain is filling. I will spray insecticide twice and herbicide once to keep the weeds and bugs down. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant summer maize on the same 6 mu without ploughing again — no-tillage saves time and diesel. I will sow *denghai605*, a hybrid maize, one package per mu. Maize grows fast in the summer heat; I will irrigate it twice and fertilize it with compound fertilizer at planting, then add urea at the jointing stage. I will spray insecticide twice and herbicide once. I expect about 1,100 jin of grain per mu.

I will also plant 2 mu of cotton with *guoxinmian* because the cotton price has been steady and it gives me cash income in the autumn. Cotton needs rotary tillage, two irrigations, and a lot of spraying — I have to watch the bollworms carefully, so I will spray insecticide about 13 times and herbicide once. I expect roughly 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.
